Let’s talk about something that makes all the difference in the long run—how to keep your success going strong.
This is Chapter 10: Sustaining Success—Building Habits for the Long Run.
So, how do you actually make all these new strategies stick, day in and day out?
The truth is, high achievement isn’t about one huge push. It’s about creating simple, steady habits that, over time, become almost automatic.
The first big idea here? Start small. Instead of trying to change everything at once, focus on just one or two new habits at a time.
Imagine this: maybe you set a fixed time to study every evening. Once that feels natural, you might add something like active recall, or taking a few minutes for regular reflection.
These little wins build your confidence—and before long, you’ve got some real momentum.
Now, let’s be real. Consistency matters way more than perfection. You’ll have days when things don’t go as planned—and that’s okay. What sets high performers apart is that they get back on track as soon as possible.
Maybe you use reminders on your phone, checklists, or even a friend to keep you accountable. And if you slip up? You forgive yourself and keep moving forward.
Here’s something else to keep in mind: building good habits isn’t a “set it and forget it” deal. Life changes. New classes, jobs, or responsibilities come up. The most successful students review how their routines are working and make little tweaks along the way, so their habits always fit what’s happening in their lives.
So, if you want habits that truly last, here’s what to do:
First, pick just one or two habits to focus on, so you don’t get overwhelmed.
Second, use reminders or accountability buddies to help you stay consistent.
Third, check in with yourself and adjust your routines when life throws you a curveball.
And finally, be patient with yourself. Setbacks happen, but that doesn’t mean you’re off track for good.
When you build these steps into your daily life, you set yourself up for a self-sustaining cycle of achievement—and a sense of well-being that lasts.
